government.note: Parliamentary republic under the 1998 Constitution. The President is elected by the unicameral Parliament (Kuvendi) by secret ballot for a five-year term: a three-fifths majority of all members is needed in the first three ballots, after which a fourth ballot is limited to the two leading candidates. The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers and is responsible to Parliament.

offices.note: During a vacancy or incapacity the Speaker of Parliament exercises the President's powers.

system.note: Since 2009: 140 members elected by closed-list proportional representation in 12 multi-member constituencies matching the counties (threshold 3% for parties and 5% for pre-election coalitions within a constituency; the formula is not stated in the fetched source). The 1997 and 2001-2005 parliaments used a mixed system (single-member constituencies plus national list seats); the 1997 parliament had 155 members (115 constituency and 40 list seats). seats_2000 is the result of the June-July 1997 election; the article's text says 151 seats, but its results table sums to 155. Changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the June 1997 national list (PR) vote (shares computed from the vote counts): Socialist Party 52.8% and Social Democratic Party 2.5% (social democrat), Democratic Party 25.7% (liberal conservative; the party article lists conservatism), Republican Party 2.4% and the Albanian National Front 2.4% (national conservative), Legality Movement 3.3% (constitutional monarchist), Unity for Human Rights 2.8% (regionalist: Greek minority party), Democratic Alliance 2.7% (centrist liberal), Demochristian Party 1.0% (Christian democrat), Agrarian Party 0.8% (agrarian); remaining lists (about 3.7%) as big tent. The Socialist Party led the government in 2000 with smaller allies, which are not recorded as ruling parties here.
